slides.0.title: Other fortified wines: VDN, Rutherglen and Marsala
slides.0.subtitle: All fortified, but each place tells a different story with its own grapes and ageing
slides.1.title: French vins doux naturels (VDN)
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Muscat styles
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Such as Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise and Muscat de Rivesaltes: mutage mid-fermentation keeps grapey aroma and sweetness; usually drunk young for fresh floral fruit
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Grenache styles
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Banyuls, Maury, Rivesaltes: either bottled young reductively (Rimage, Grenat) or aged oxidatively in casks or sun-exposed glass demijohns, developing rancio character (Tuilé, Ambré, Hors d’âge)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Comparison with Port
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Both are sweet reds fortified mid-fermentation: Port blends many varieties with fast extraction, while Banyuls and Maury are Grenache-based; both have reductive and oxidative paths
slides.1.content: VDN’s keyword is mutage: the same principle as Port, with different grapes and terroir.
slides.2.title: Rutherglen Muscat
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Region and variety
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Rutherglen in north-east Victoria, Australia, fortifies late-picked, overripe red-skinned Muscat à Petits Grains, then ages it for years in casks in hot tin sheds
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Four-tier classification
slides.2.highlights.1.content: From youngest to oldest: Rutherglen, Classic, Grand, Rare; the higher the tier, the older the average age and the richer the wine, with toffee, coffee, raisin and fig
slides.2.highlights.2.title: The role of heat
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Hot sheds speed oxidation and evaporation, concentrating sugar, acid and flavour, on a similar principle to Madeira’s heated ageing
slides.2.content: Rutherglen is the New World’s signature fortified wine: its tiers translate age into language consumers understand.
slides.3.title: Marsala
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Region and varieties
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Western Sicily; the white Oro and Ambra use Grillo, Catarratto and Inzolia, the red Rubino uses Perricone, Nero d’Avola and others; Ambra may include cooked concentrated must (mosto cotto)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Age categories
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Fine at least 1 year, Superiore 2, Superiore Riserva 4, Vergine (Soleras) 5, Vergine Stravecchio (Riserva) 10; Vergine must be dry and contain no mosto cotto
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Image and revival
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Marsala was long treated as a cooking wine and its image suffered; a few producers are rebuilding its reputation with quality dry styles such as Vergine, a good example of how category image can drag down quality
slides.3.content: The essay angle on Marsala resembles Sherry: a volume image holds it back, premium dry styles drive the revival.
